significance.root_decision: The congruence holds for every m >= 1 and every n > 1 with n ≡ 1 (mod 4). Closest prior work: the block values in Guo's source, the base case from Guo and Zudilin (2020), and Guo's 2020 arbitrary-m result for n ≡ 3 (mod 4); the arbitrary-m statement modulo the square of the cyclotomic polynomial for n ≡ 1 (mod 4) was left open as Conjecture 6.2. The proof splits the left side into blocks of length n, shows that each block agrees with the right side's base value at every primitive n-th root of unity to first order (value and derivative), using a reciprocity under a shift of a parameter and a cancellation of the first-order shift errors between complementary blocks, and proves the base block by a terminating Dixon-type identity with an explicit WZ-style certificate. Lean works in the field of rational functions over Q with q the variable, states the congruence as coprimality of both denominators with Φ_n together with divisibility of the numerator of the difference by Φ_n^2, proves every denominator in the statement nonzero, and proves the base case rather than assuming it.
significance.caveat: Borderline significance: the reflection-at-roots toolkit is standard in this school and is shared with Liu and Tao (arXiv:2606.12037), which works at the level of values; the new content is the first-order shift-error cancellation for arbitrary m. The cross-model reviewer puts 0.55 on not routine and 0.60 on the verdict, at the floor root uses for counting. Prior-art clearance is bounded (access limits documented). No second cross-model lane read the finished Lean: root compared the final theorem and every definition with the endpoint the Claude Opus reviewer had written (identical), and the GPT-6.1 Sol final check verified nine exact cases modulo Φ_n^2 and their failure modulo Φ_n^3.
